caption_short: The end-of-session recognition path in PEERS: after studying 16 lists of 16 words and doing immediate free recall, subjects take an item-recognition test with confidence judgements (and, in half the sessions, a 5-minute final free-recall test first).

notes: This is the SAME Figure 1 as peers_recall.png, not a separate figure. The paper contains no dedicated panel or screenshot of the recognition response screen or of the confidence scale, so per instructions this crop is the sub-region of Figure 1 (the Experiments 1 and 3 row) that contains the 'Item Recognition with Conf. Judgments' branch; use peers_recall.png if a single shared figure is preferred. Recognition procedure per the paper's Methods ('Measuring Recognition'): responses were vocal - subjects said 'pess' or 'po' instead of 'yes'/'no' so that the stop consonant gave precise response timing - and confidence ratings were collected after the old/new decision; subjects were incentivised for speed on the yes/no response and for accuracy via the confidence judgement. The paper does not state the number of confidence levels in this figure or its caption. Cropped from a 220-dpi render of p. 32.
